# UVEITIS

Most cases are non-infectious. Most infectious cases are associated with a pathogen causing systemic or central nervous system infection. Diagnosis of uveitis usually must be made presumptively due to the technical difficulty of sampling the uvea. Cases have been associated with fungi, bacteria, viruses, and protozoa like Toxoplasma gondii.

# For treatment of posterior uveitis (retinitis) or acute retinal necrosis (ARN) due to Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) or herpes simplex virus (HSV) or Cytomegalovirus (CMV)
